records.preparationDescription: Culinary use, not treatment: duhat fruits are eaten fresh or processed into juice, sauces, jams and preserves. The source supplies no diabetes-treatment recipe.
historicalExclusions: Do not substitute seed powder, bark or leaf tea for diabetes treatment.

records.preparationDescription: Culinary use, not treatment: the tart pulp is used as a flavouring in curries, chutneys, jams, confectionery and beverages. No medicinal laxative dose or timed recipe is established.
historicalExclusions: Do not present historical laxative doses as current clinical guidance.

records.preparationDescription: Culinary use, not treatment: mature fruit is eaten fresh or added to smoothies and desserts. Seeds must be removed before serving; the source identifies them as toxic when swallowed.
historicalExclusions: Withhold seed scalp-pest recipes and prevent seed exposure to eyes.

records.preparationDescription: NParks identifies the kernel as food, but the reviewed page gives no preparation method. Do not invent roasting, boiling or medicinal tea instructions to fill this field.
historicalExclusions: Withhold unsupported leaf-tea and bark treatment recipes.

records.preparationDescription: Culinary use, not treatment: flowers supply an edible blue colour extract used in traditional Malay pastries. The reviewed source gives no extraction time, ratio or therapeutic flower-tea regimen.
historicalExclusions: Withhold the historical root and seed purgative recipes.

records.preparationDescription: Culinary use, not treatment: the edible ripe fruit has juicy yellow flesh. The reviewed page does not specify a cooking recipe; do not manufacture a leaf or bark decoction from its list of folk claims.
historicalExclusions: Withhold unvalidated bark, resin, seed and leaf treatments.

records.preparationDescription: Culinary use, not treatment: the whitish pulp is eaten fresh or made into marmalade and candy. Medicinal bark and root instructions are not cleared by this food description.
historicalExclusions: Do not recommend swallowing santol seeds; retain the existing human-injury safety hold.

records.preparationPart: Fruit flesh only in this proposed description
records.preparationDescription: Culinary use, not treatment: papaya fruit is eaten, made into jellies or preserves, or cooked as a vegetable. This food description does not establish dengue treatment or a latex preparation.
historicalExclusions: Withhold latex, seed, root and leaf medicinal regimens; retain part-specific pregnancy and child safety review.

records.preparationDescription: Culinary use, not treatment: the fruit pulp is eaten fresh or processed into juice, jellies and syrups. This does not establish a root-bark worm treatment.
historicalExclusions: Withhold root, stem and peel regimens; NCCIH warns that large amounts of those materials can be harmful.

records.preparationPart: Fruit flesh, not seed kernels or sap
records.preparationDescription: Culinary use, not treatment: edible fruit is eaten fresh or used in desserts. The same source flags irritating sap and toxic seed ingestion, so no seed preparation is included.
historicalExclusions: Withhold seed paste and immature-fruit medicinal regimens; a seed injury threshold is not a safe dose.
